outcome: No source found reports the Fontaine–Mazur conjectures as a whole proved or disproved since 26 January 2024; the movement is in sub-cases: a preprint whose latest version (7 October 2026) claims the regular two-dimensional case over Q for all odd primes and credits GPT 6 Astra with repairing an error and helping change the proof strategy; a claimed irregular residually reducible case over Q (same date); new GL2 cases over totally real fields with ordinary Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} (August 2026); and reformulations of Boston's unramified generalisation (April 2024, January 2026).
problem_asks: The Wikipedia lead says the Fontaine–Mazur conjectures are 'some conjectures introduced by Fontaine and Mazur' (1995), concerning when p-adic representations of Galois groups of number fields come from étale cohomology of varieties. Parts, as the sources state them: (1) Geometric implies from geometry: every irreducible continuous p-adic representation of the absolute Galois group of a number field K that is unramified outside finitely many places and potentially semistable at each place above p arises from étale cohomology of a variety over K. The converse (algebro-geometric representations are potentially semistable) is recorded in a search snippet of a 2020s survey as known (Tsuji) and is not part of what is open. (2) Over Q, the first conjecture as the Wikipedia lead states it: an irreducible representation unramified outside finitely many primes and not a Tate twist of an even representation with finite image corresponds to a cuspidal newform exactly when it is potentially semistable at p. (3) The two-dimensional odd case over Q: an odd irreducible geometric representation with distinct Hodge–Tate weights at p is modular (a twist of a newform of weight k at least 2). (4) The even case: the conjecture predicts that the relevant even two-dimensional representations do not exist. (5) The cases with equal Hodge–Tate weights (irregular) and residually reducible representations, which the general statement does not exclude. (6) Over totally real fields (the form stated as Conjecture A in Thorne 2026): GL2 representations unramified almost everywhere, de Rham at each p-adic place with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and totally odd determinant arise from geometry. (7) The unramified version: an irreducible representation unramified everywhere has finite image. Luo (2024) describes this as a special case of the Fontaine–Mazur family. Boston's generalisation (continuous homomorphisms into GL_n over complete Noetherian local rings with finite residue field have finite image) is Boston's own conjecture, recorded here as a related generalisation rather than part of the statement. (8) The group-theoretic reading in the Wikipedia lead: infinite ℓ-adic analytic groups cannot occur as Galois groups of unramified ℓ-extensions of number fields. (9) A tame variant named by Feuerpfeil (2026) as 'the tame Fontaine–Mazur Conjecture', predicting that certain groups have no nontrivial uniformly powerful pro-p quotients. Whether it is one of the 'numerous conjectures' in the Wikipedia statement was not established. The original 1995 paper was not accessed, so the enumeration rests on the Wikipedia lead and on the secondary sources cited against each part.

events.what_happened: Nigel Boston, 'Some cases of the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture, II', arXiv:math/9808145. Abstract (opened): 'We prove more special cases of the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture regarding p-adic Galois representations unramified at p, and we present evidence for and consequences of a generalization of it.' The generalization is Boston's Conjecture 2 (finite image over complete Noetherian local rings), as recorded in Luo (2024).

events.remains: Every part of problem_asks outside the unramified-at-p special cases, and Boston's generalisation itself.

events.what_happened: Xinyao Zhang, 'On the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture for p=3', arXiv:2412.06812 (single author; University of Tokyo per search snippet). v1 (30 Nov 2024, opened): 'In this article, we prove some new cases of the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture on two-dimensional Galois representations'; and 'Combining the previous work, we can conclude the conjecture in the regular case when p is an odd prime.' v4 (22 Jul 2025) and v5 (7 Oct 2026, marked 'Major change', opened) state the result as: the remaining p=3 cases of the regular two-dimensional conjecture over Q are proved, which completes the regular case for all odd primes. The main theorem (v5, Theorem 1.0.2 as paraphrased): p an odd prime; ρ: Gal(Q̄/Q)→GL2(Q̄p) continuous, irreducible, ramified at finitely many places, de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights at p, odd; then ρ arises from a cuspidal eigenform up to twist. Pan's Theorem 1.0.1 needed an extra assumption at p=3 on the semisimplification of ρ̄ restricted to G_Qp; Zhang drops it. The v5 abstract describes the new input as a potential big R=T theorem for large-dimensional components of global pseudo-deformation spaces.
events.revisions: v1 30 Nov 2024 ('some new cases'; regular odd-prime conclusion stated in the body); v2 19 Jan 2025; v3 22 Jan 2025; v4 22 Jul 2025; v5 7 Oct 2026 ('Major change'; acknowledgement credits GPT 6 Astra; see ai). Abstract wording changed across versions; the regular odd-prime claim appears in v1.

events.what_happened: Jack A. Thorne, 'Towards the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture for GL(2)', arXiv:2608.07186 (single version, v1, 7 Aug 2026; opened abstract page; HTML partly read). Abstract (opened): 'We combine a new type of modularity result with the geometry of numbers' to 'prove some new cases of the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture for GL(2)'. From the introduction and theorem statements in the HTML: Conjecture A (totally real F, continuous irreducible ρ: G_F→GL2(Q̄p), unramified at almost all places, de Rham at each p-adic place with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, totally odd determinant, conclusion: arises from geometry, i.e. from an algebraic variety X over F). Theorem B (totally real F, ρ irreducible, unramified almost everywhere, potentially crystalline and ordinary with Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} at each p-adic place, totally odd determinant; conclusion: potentially modular). Theorem D (over Q, same ordinary weights {0,1}, odd determinant; conclusion: modular). The introduction says earlier methods required the residual representation to be non-degenerate and that the residually reducible gap is the target.
events.delivers: New cases of Conjecture A for GL2 over totally real fields, in the ordinary case with Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} (Theorem B: potential modularity; Theorem D: modularity over Q). Whether Theorem B yields Conjecture A's geometric conclusion in these cases is what the paper's deduction is for; the deduction was not read. Restricted to ordinary weights {0,1}.
events.remains: Non-ordinary cases and other Hodge–Tate weights for totally real fields; the general statement; the non-ordinary and general-weight parts of Conjecture A.

events.what_happened: Julian Feuerpfeil, 'Bockstein Spectral Sequences and Applications to the Tame Fontaine Mazur Conjecture', arXiv:2608.10811 (v1, 11 Aug 2026; math.NT, cross-listed math.GR; opened abstract page). Abstract (opened, summarised): for a number field K, prime p and finite set S of tame places, studies the maximal pro-p extension unramified outside S; extends Labute's method using Bockstein spectral sequences and Lie-theoretic tools; checks the uniform Fontaine–Mazur property for infinitely many such groups with |S|=3 under mild conditions on K; identifies a large class of infinite groups; reports numerical evidence. The page gives the tame conjecture only as: these groups have no nontrivial uniformly powerful pro-p quotients.
events.delivers: A group-theoretic result for the tame variant with |S|=3 (no nontrivial uniform quotients for infinitely many such S, under mild conditions on K). It is an analogue of the statement in a different setting (tame ramification, pro-p groups), not a case of the Galois-representation statement.
events.remains: The Galois-representation statement in every part; the tame variant for other S and in general.
events.time_since_posted: 2 months before the record date; no engagement found.
events.doubts: Numerical evidence is stated as probabilistic ('very high probability') for |S|=3 and does not prove the statement.
events.direction: Neutral on the Galois statement: analogue in the tame, pro-p group setting.

events.what_happened: Xinyao Zhang, 'Modular points and dimensions of Eisenstein deformation spaces', arXiv:2512.21249 v3 (7 Oct 2026, marked 'Major change'; abstract page and HTML partly read). Abstract (opened): studies two-dimensional Eisenstein deformation spaces; over Q under generic hypotheses, irreducible components have characteristic zero and dimension 4; modular points are Zariski dense; a big R=T theorem; Mazur's dimension conjecture over Q; and 'we establish the irregular Fontaine–Mazur conjecture in the residually reducible, multiplicity-free case for p≥5', and for p=3 outside one explicit local dihedral case. Theorem 1.2.2 (HTML, read): p>2; ρ: G_Q→GL2(Q̄p) continuous, irreducible, unramified outside finitely many primes, odd; Hodge–Tate weights {0,0} at p; ρ̄ semisimplification χ̄1⊕χ̄2 with χ̄1≠χ̄2; and either (χ̄1/χ̄2)|G_Qp ≠ ω^±1 or ρ|G_Qp reducible. Conclusion: ρ is modular of weight one with finite image. For p≥5 the last condition is automatic; the remaining p=3 case is an explicit locally induced case.

Conclusion: modular weight one, finite image.

The claim is new in this version (not in v1 or v2 per their abstracts), its argument has not been checked by anyone else in the sources found, and the abstract's own qualification (one local dihedral case at p=3 excluded) means it is not the full conjecture even for Q.

events.what_happened: Three manuscripts in the family; two bear directly on this problem. (a) “Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2” (FM2) claims in Theorem 1.1 that every continuous, irreducible, odd two-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ, unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, is isomorphic to a Tate twist of the 2-adic representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform. Its abstract says this resolves the odd, regular two-dimensional Fontaine–Mazur conjecture over ℚ at 2, including all residual representations. The argument has three stages: potential pro-modularity over a solvable totally real field F of even degree, split completely at 2, obtained by connectedness and patching from a modular seed (Theorem thm:potential-promodularity); production of a locally algebraic vector with the target eigensystem, using ordinary families and Thorne's Theorem D in the reducible local case and the local Langlands correspondence in the absolutely irreducible local case; and descent from a regular algebraic Hilbert cusp form over F, obtained by Jacquet–Langlands from a definite quaternion algebra, to ℚ by cyclic descent with a finite-character twist. The introduction adds that the geometric realization of modular representations gives the geometric-origin conclusion in this setting; the body does not argue that. (b) “Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two” (UPM2) claims, with no de Rham or residual hypothesis, that every continuous odd absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in the full completed two-adic Hecke algebra 𝕋₂(N) at some odd level N: there is a continuous ℤ₂-algebra map λ: 𝕋₂(N) → O_E with λ(T_ℓ) = tr r(Frob_ℓ) and λ(ℓS_ℓ) = det r(Frob_ℓ). It states that it does not assert classical modularity. Its proof places r in a fixed-determinant trace family, finds an auxiliary regular de Rham point x, applies FM2's Theorem 1.1 to x to get classicality, and then uses the dimension theorem of (c) and Newton–Thorne's adjoint Selmer vanishing to show the original point lies on Hecke support (conclusion.tex, proof of Theorem main). (c) “The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level” (DHA) claims that for every odd N every irreducible component of Spec 𝕋₂(N) has Krull dimension exactly 4, the p = 2 case of Emerton's dimension conjecture. It makes no claim about Galois modularity; it bears on this problem only as an input to UPM2.
events.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Unrestricted-pro-modularity-at-the-prime-two-October-4-2026, Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-September-23-2026
events.delivers: For the list's Fontaine–Mazur problem, FM2 proves, at p = 2 only, the odd, regular, two-dimensional case over ℚ: an odd, irreducible, two-dimensional 2-adic representation, de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and unramified outside finitely many primes, is modular up to Tate twist (a classical cuspidal eigenform). The residual representation is unrestricted, and scalar and reducible residual cases are included. This corresponds to the list's part (3), restricted to dimension two, odd, regular, and at 2, and to the modularity half of part (2) in that case. The list's part (3) matches FM2's statement, apart from the prime, which is 2 only. The list's part (2) uses ‘potentially semistable at p’ and FM2 uses ‘de Rham at 2’; the text passes from de Rham to potentially semistable by citing Berger (lemma dense-Thorne-points). The geometric-origin conclusion of part (1) is asserted in one sentence of the introduction and not proved in the body. FM2's introduction says that, together with odd-prime results discussed there (Pan 2022; Zhang 2025 for p = 3), the theorem gives the modularity conclusion ‘at every prime’. Those odd-prime results are other papers, and this family proves only p = 2. UPM2 delivers less: occurrence in a completed Hecke algebra for every odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation, with no Hodge–Tate or de Rham condition. It delivers no classical modularity for any representation, so it does not give the conjecture's conclusion. DHA delivers no Galois-theoretic conclusion. The manuscripts claim to resolve the odd regular two-dimensional case over ℚ at 2, not the conjecture as a whole. None of them addresses the even case, the equal-Hodge–Tate-weight case, totally real base fields, the unramified-everywhere / finite-image statement, the group-theoretic reading, or the tame variant.
events.remains: If the claims hold, the following stay open for the list's problem: (i) every prime other than 2 within this family, since the every-prime statement depends on external odd-prime papers; (ii) the even two-dimensional case, where the conjecture predicts nonexistence; (iii) the equal-Hodge–Tate-weight (irregular) case for classical modularity, where UPM2 gives only occurrence; (iv) general dimension, general number fields, and the geometric-origin conclusion beyond the one-sentence claim; (v) totally real base fields (list item 6); (vi) the unramified-everywhere / finite-image statement (item 7), the group-theoretic reading (item 8), and the tame variant (item 9); (vii) classical modularity of the representations that UPM2 shows occur in the completed Hecke algebra, which UPM2 says it does not assert.
events.doubts: FM2: (1) The geometric-origin conclusion is asserted in a single sentence of the introduction with no argument in the body, which ends at ‘classical cuspidal eigenform’. (2) The reducible local branch rests on Thorne's 2026 preprint (Theorem D), which is cited as the source of modularity for its dense ordinary points. (3) The every-prime claim in the introduction depends on odd-prime results outside the family. (4) The virtually solvable case (Lemma solvable-reduction) is argued in about sixty lines: the imaginary quadratic subcase is handled by citing theta series and Jacquet–Langlands, and the real quadratic subcase by a unit-theorem argument. (5) I read the statements and key steps of the classicality, connectedness and preliminaries sections; I did not read the patching, deformation, completed_forms or fields sections in full, and checked them only by grep for hedging language. I did not check the proofs in detail. UPM2: (1) Its main theorem is occurrence, not classicality, so it inherits every dependency on FM2 and DHA. (2) Thorne's Theorem D is named in the introduction as an essential input, but I found no body section citing it. (3) The marked-line, transverse-chart and Selmer-loss construction for the scalar and reducible-residue branches is described in the introduction; I read the introduction and the regular-point section (lines 1–60, 330–404) in full and grepped family.tex, diagonal.tex and hecke.tex for citations and hedging words only, so those branches are checked only at the level of the introduction. DHA: (1) The lower bound (every component has dimension at least 4) is quoted from Emerton's Corollary 2.28 ‘with p = 2’. The text says its own determinant argument supplies the p = 2 justification for Emerton's Theorem 2.7, which had an odd-prime restriction; whether that repair also covers Corollary 2.28 is asserted, not separately shown. (2) The Selmer-vanishing input, Newton–Thorne Theorem 5.4 specialised to GL₂/ℚ, is stated to include p = 2 and a CM condition. The cited paper's title, ‘Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type’, is about unitary-type groups, so the specialisation carries real weight in the argument.; conditional on: FM2's Theorem 1.1 relies on cited results it does not prove. Thorne, ‘Towards the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture for GL₂’ (arXiv:2608.07186v1, a 2026 preprint), Theorem D, is used in the reducible local branch to make dense ordinary points modular (lemma dense-Thorne-points); this is the main external dependency. Other inputs are BLGGT 2014 Theorem 2.1.1 (Galois representations for Hilbert cusp forms at 2), Colmez 2010 and Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas 2014 (local p-adic Langlands at 2), Berger 2002 (de Rham implies potentially semistable), Jacquet–Langlands and Arthur–Clozel (base change and descent), and Billerey–Menares 2016 for the existence of cuspidal lifts in the reducible-residue connectedness step, which the manuscript says it re-proves in detail. UPM2 is conditional on FM2 (Theorem 1.1 applied to its auxiliary point, and the curve and connectedness arguments it takes from FM2), on DHA (its dimension-four theorem), on Newton–Thorne 2023 Theorem 5.4 as specialised to GL₂/ℚ, and on Allen 2016 Lemma 1.1.3. Its introduction also cites Thorne's Theorem D as supplying an essential set of classical points, but I found no body section that cites Thorne. DHA is conditional on Emerton's Corollary 2.28 (the lower bound of dimension 4) and on Newton–Thorne Theorem 5.4 as specialised to GL₂/ℚ at p = 2.
events.direction: proves a case: odd, regular, two-dimensional over ℚ at p = 2, classical modularity up to Tate twist; plus a weaker occurrence-only pro-modularity result for all odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional cases at 2

summary: Found: no source reports the Fontaine–Mazur conjectures as a whole settled, and I have not classified the problem. The only status label found is the ProofAtlas tracker's 'Partially resolved' (opened; a research workspace whose footer reads 'AI-first mathematical research'; it attributes no step to any AI system and names no contributor, so it is a lead, not evidence). Since January 2024 the mathematics that bears on the statement is in sub-cases. (1) Zhang, arXiv:2412.06812 (first posted 30 Nov 2024; latest v5 posted 7 Oct 2026, 'Major change'). The v1 body (opened) says 'Combining the previous work, we can conclude the conjecture in the regular case when p is an odd prime'; v5 (opened) claims the remaining p=3 cases over Q, completing the regular case for all odd primes, and removes an extra p=3 hypothesis in Pan's theorem. The v5 acknowledgement reads (in two fragments of the HTML) 'The author would like to thank GPT 6 Astra for pointing out a serious error in an earlier version of Proposition 2.3.3 ... and helping him to modify the strategy of the proof in Section 5.' This is the only AI credit I found in the whole record, and it is the close call. Reading one: catching an error is checking, which DEEP_DIVE §5.4 excludes from ai.systems. Reading two: a model-suggested change of proof strategy in the section the argument turns on is load-bearing, and the authors credit it as such. I recorded it under ai.systems with the authors' sentence and left the weighing to the later pass. The paper does not say what the new strategy is, or how much of the revised argument came from the model. The name 'GPT 6 Astra' is as the source gives it; secondary reports (QZ, Forklog, SiliconANGLE; search snippets, not opened in full) describe Astra as an internal OpenAI model that produced math results in August 2026, later released, so which build was used is unknown. OpenAI's primary Astra pages returned HTTP 403, and the secondary lists of Astra's August 2026 results contain no Fontaine–Mazur or Galois-representation result, so none of them is an event here. (2) Zhang, arXiv:2512.21249. v1 (24 Dec 2025) and v2 (1 Jan 2026) use the conjecture only as an input, which I opened in the abstract. v3 (7 Oct 2026, retitled) claims the irregular conjecture (Hodge–Tate weights {0,0}) in the residually reducible multiplicity-free case for p≥5, and for p=3 except one explicit local dihedral case; the conclusion is modularity of weight one with finite image. I read most of the v3 HTML and found no AI mention in what I read. (3) Thorne, arXiv:2608.07186 (single version, 7 Aug 2026): new cases of Conjecture A for GL2 over totally real fields with ordinary Hodge–Tate weights {0,1} (Theorem B: potential modularity; Theorem D over Q). The text read contains no AI mention; I did not read the end. (4) Luo, arXiv:2404.18967 (29 Apr 2024) and arXiv:2601.20395 (28 Jan 2026): work on Boston's unramified generalisation, not the geometric statement; the 2024 paper's conditional counterexamples are to the dimension conjecture, and both papers are v1 and unreviewed. (5) Feuerpfeil, arXiv:2608.10811 (11 Aug 2026): a tame, pro-p group analogue, which I record as an analogue. (6) Older events (predating the window) are recorded with dates: Boston 1998; Chojecki 2013 (Padova 2018); Kisin 2009 (JAMS); Calegari 2009 (Inventiones 2011; II in JAMS 2012 per snippet); Paškūnas 2016; Pan 2019 (JAMS 2022); Tung 2019; Ahlqvist–Carlson 2022 (Crelle 2025, which does not mention Fontaine–Mazur and whose 2025 talk calls its examples the 'last remaining case' of the unramified conjecture). Not recorded as events because they were seen only in search snippets: Dieulefait 2004 (Wikipedia lead), Emerton's local–global compatibility work (around 2010–2011), Hu–Tan's Breuil–Mézard proof (2015, which removes a restriction in the FM argument), Calegari–Geraghty 2012 (first results on Boston's generalisation per Luo's citation), Zhang's pro-modularity preprint arXiv:2411.18661 (Nov 2024), and a 2025 Breuil–Mézard search result. Where a call was close: (a) the GPT 6 Astra credit; (b) whether Thorne's Theorem B gives the geometric conclusion of Conjecture A in the ordinary case, which I could not read; (c) whether Zhang's p=3 v5 repair (Proposition 2.3.3 and Section 5) is sound, which nobody I could find has checked.
competing_reading: The regular two-dimensional case of the first conjecture over Q could be read as settled for all odd primes: Pan (2019 arXiv, JAMS 2022) covers p at least 5 and, with Zhang's v5 (October 2026), p=3 without the extra hypothesis. Against that, v5 is four days old, labels itself 'Major change', and repairs an error the author says was found with AI help in an earlier version of the same argument; so the p=3 completion rests on an unreviewed repaired proof. Pan's own paper is refereed, but the p=3 step is not the one Pan's journal version checked. The AI credit could be read as proofreading (excluded by §5.4), which would make the record's only AI involvement incidental; the acknowledgement's 'helping him to modify the strategy of the proof in Section 5' is the reading that makes it load-bearing.
what_would_settle_it: (a) An expert check of arXiv:2412.06812 v5, specifically the repaired Proposition 2.3.3 and the Section 5 argument, and a publication or written verification of that version. (b) The author's own account of what GPT 6 Astra supplied (a changelog, a note, or the earlier and later text of Section 5), which would settle whether the contribution is load-bearing. (c) Which OpenAI build 'GPT 6 Astra' is: the OpenAI primary page, which returned 403, or the author's statement. (d) For arXiv:2512.21249 v3: a check of the irregular residually reducible claim and its p=3 exception, and whether v2's body had the claim. (e) For arXiv:2608.07186: the deduction of Conjecture A's geometric conclusion from Theorem B, and the parts of the paper I did not read (the end of the HTML, including its references). (f) Journal status of Luo's papers (the Journal of Number Theory item with a 'Remarks' title, April 2026, is unconfirmed). (g) The original 1995 Fontaine–Mazur statements, to check the enumeration in problem_asks against the Wikipedia lead.

event.what_happened: Yufan Luo, 'On the Boston's Unramified Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture', arXiv:2404.18967 (v1 only, 29 Apr 2024; 44 pages; opened). Abstract (opened): studies the unramified Fontaine–Mazur conjecture and its generalisations; proves some basic cases and gives criteria for verifying it; proposes strategies reducing it to special cases; proves new results in the two-dimensional case; assuming the conjecture, shows the generic fibre of the unramified deformation ring is a finite product of fields; gives counterexamples to the dimension conjecture for Galois deformation rings, assuming the unramified Fontaine–Mazur conjecture.
event.delivers: Partial results for the unramified version (a special case of the family, and Boston's generalisation): basic cases, criteria, and new two-dimensional results. The deformation-ring and dimension-conjecture statements are conditional on the unramified conjecture, so they do not settle it. Does not address the geometric statement (items 1–6 of problem_asks).
event.remains: The unramified conjecture in general (Boston's generalisation in full); the geometric statement entirely.
event.time_since_posted: 2 years 5 months before the record date; no review or citing work found in the searches; Luo's second paper (2026) is by the same author and builds on it (snippet).
event.direction: Neutral to supportive: basic cases and criteria in the unramified setting; the counterexamples are to the dimension conjecture and are explicitly conditional on the unramified Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, not to that conjecture.

judgement.why: The statement names 'numerous conjectures', so every settled sub-case (the regular odd two-dimensional case over Q at a given prime, the irregular residually reducible case, the totally real ordinary weight-{0,1} cases, the even case, and the unramified cases) is a case, never the whole. Chojecki's conditional pro-modular result and Feuerpfeil's tame pro-p statement concern changed questions, so they are variants. Luo 2026, the talks and Zhang's Eisenstein v1/v2 only reformulate the conjecture or use it as an input, so they are none. Ahlqvist–Carlson does not address the conjecture. The close call is Zhang p=3. Spotting the error is criticism and earns no credit. But the acknowledgement also credits the model with 'helping him to modify the strategy of the proof in Section 5', the section the completion turns on. A strategy that the human then carried out is mathematics supplied, so I answered assisted rather than none. The OpenAI family is AI-generated by the repository's own account. Its FM2 result is the p=2 odd regular case, which is a case; it is doubtful but kept.
judgement.doubts: The Zhang p=3 credit is thin: the record cannot say how much of the new Section 5 strategy came from the model, and the attribution belongs to v5 (2026), not to the 2024 v1 date the event carries. Paškūnas's journal publication rests only on a snippet, so it is left unreviewed. The OpenAI p=2 result and Zhang's p=3 result together with Pan would cover the regular odd two-dimensional case over Q for every prime, but each piece is a separate case and none of them has been checked.
